dedupe_keys.name: bgp tools internet routing and autonomous system lookup and monitoring service

description: bgp.tools is a web service for exploring the internet's routing system, run by Port 179 Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales. Users can look up any autonomous system, prefix or IP address to see its announcements, upstream and downstream networks, peering and exchange point memberships, and related routing information collected from BGP sessions with many networks. Core lookup features are free to use, while paid plans add monitoring and alerting for a network's own prefixes and ASNs, for example on route hijacks, leaks or visibility changes. Coverage: the global routing table and internet exchange points. Format and access: website, free for core lookups, with paid monitoring subscriptions; bulk or automated access is governed by the site's terms. Caveats: a commercial service whose data collection, retention and methods are its own; the feature details here come from a fetched summary of the home page. Simulation uses: mapping the upstream dependencies of networks in a country or sector, checking how exchange and transit failures would affect reachability, and tracking routing incidents. Related records: RIPEstat, Kentik and BGPStream are other routing tools, and PeeringDB and the CAIDA IXPs dataset describe exchange membership.
